title: A workflow failure report reached you: what it says and what to do
summary: When a package's verdict is WARN, FAIL or ERROR, the Workflow writes one message for the lane that submitted it and posts it to the Rasen Falcon mailbox: a reply when it knows the request that submitted the package, otherwise a new request on the lane. The subject reads 'Workflow <verdict> for <package>: <n> to fix, <m> warning(s)'. The body starts with the credits and the command that sets up the environment, then lists every FAIL as a numbered entry: the step and its version, the rule id, the layer of the rule book that set its severity, where (file:line), what was found, the fix, and the command that shows that one finding again (with --only <step> --again). The WARNs follow; they do not stop the build. A chat is told by a one-sentence nudge that carries no content, only that the report is in its mailbox. In shadow mode (now) every FAIL is reported as a WARN whose severity line says it is a FAIL when enforced.
invariants: Fix exactly what the report names. Do not rewrite unrelated code in the same submission.
An ERROR section means the Workflow itself broke on that step. That is not your package's fault: report it on the lane the message came from and carry on.
A resubmission with an identical tree is not run again; it gets the same receipt. Change the package before resubmitting.
A rule can be relaxed only by a written line in the rule book, in the layer it applies to, with a comment giving the reason. Ask Tom; do not edit etc/house.rules yourself.
The command lines in the report are meant to be run as they are, from the repository root, after sourcing workflow_env.sh. They end without a period.
procedure: Read the whole report in the mailbox, not just the nudge.
For each numbered FAIL: open file:line, apply the fix, run its 'check it yourself' command and see the finding gone.
Resubmit, and reply on the report's thread with what you changed, credits included.
If you think a finding is wrong, reply with the evidence (the line, and why the rule should not apply). A false finding is a defect in the step and is fixed there.

provenance.claim: The body of the report: credits, environment command, numbered FAILs, then WARNs, each with where, found, fix and the command.
A report with a parent request is posted as a reply, otherwise as a new request on its lane; a posted report moves to sent, a refused one stays with its error.
Report mode makes a FAIL a WARN and says so; the reproduce command is --only <step> --again.
